newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX index closes at record high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX index closes at record high.

text.p: Hungarian share prices rebounded from an early dip on Monday to finish at their fourth successive closing high on the back of new demand, traders said.
"I think early dips were linked to psychology, as many market participants might have thought that some correction has to come after so much of a rise," one trader said.
"But later they realised there were enough buying orders to support prices."
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 7,197.82 points, up 48.79. Last week the BUX index rose more than five percent.
Traders said Hungary's potential NATO membership seems to attract fresh capital to the market.
"The market expects some information on Tuesday or Wednesday about Hungary's NATO membership," the trader said.
Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic are expected to get invitations to join NATO at a Madrid summit this week.
The volume of traded stocks and compensation coupons amounted to 2,039,358 units, bolstered by agency crosses.
BUX futures traded firmer on Monday, finishing 120 to 185 points up from Friday's settlement prices and increasing the interest content.
"Interest contents seem to become more attractive," said Tamas Petheo, trader of Buda-Cash Brokerhaz.
September BUX finished at 7,400 points, up 130, bringing its interest content above 14 percent from Friday's 8.35 percent.
On Monday, tight liquidity drove tinned food maker Globus to a 52-week high of 2,450 forints, before it retreated to end at 2,400, up 300.
Tight liquidity and news of the launch of a two billion forint investment by pharmaceuticals Human pushed its price to a new record high of 3,890 forints. It finished at 3,890, up 280.
Heavyweight chemicals TVK and pharmaceuticals Egis also hit new highs of 3,640 forints and 13,650 forints, before they eased to finish at 3,630, up 90 and at 13,650, up 350, respectively.
